content:
A raise can fix a pay problem. 
It cant fix six months of feeling ignored. 

I've spent more than 40 years working with business owners, and Ive watched some very good employees walk out the door. 

The resignation was rarely the first sign. 

They stopped bringing ideas to meetings. Good work became expected. Promised conversations kept getting pushed back. Opportunities to grow went somewhere else. 

Then the resignation comes and suddenly everyone wants to talk. 

Sometimes more money keeps them. 

Sometimes the decision was made months ago. 

Good people want fair pay, but they also want respect, responsibility, and a reason to believe they're going somewhere. 

The best time to give them that isn't when they're halfway out the door. 

Strong businesses keep good people by giving them reasons to stay long before they need one. 

The Empowered Business Fast Track Course gives business owners a practical framework for building the team, leadership, systems, and accountability needed to grow without carrying everything themselves.

comment: Retention issues often become visible too late because companies measure outcomes, not engagement signals. Regular career conversations and meaningful ownership can prevent many resignations before compensation becomes the only lever.
